details:
**Death of Baldr by mistletoe**
Loki engineered the death of Baldr, Odin and Frigg's beloved son. Frigg had made everything in creation swear not to harm Baldr except the mistletoe, a fact Loki learned by disguising himself as an old woman. He then gave a mistletoe dart, spear, or arrow to Baldr's blind brother Hodr and guided his aim, killing Baldr.

**Giving birth to Sleipnir**
When a giant mason was building the walls of Asgard with the help of his stallion Svadilfari, and was about to win the sun, the moon, and Freya as payment, Loki turned himself into a mare to lure the horse away so the walls would go unfinished. Loki later gave birth to the eight-legged horse Sleipnir, which became Odin's steed, so Loki is the "mother" of Sleipnir.

**Bound beneath a venom-dripping serpent**
As punishment for Baldr's death, the gods bound Loki to a rock using the entrails of his son Narfi (or Nari), who had been torn apart by Loki's other son Vali after Vali was turned into a wolf. The giantess Skadi fastened a serpent above him whose venom drips onto his face. His faithful wife Sigyn catches the venom in a bowl, but when she leaves to empty it, the poison hits him and his writhing causes earthquakes. He stays bound until Ragnarok.

**Fenrir, Jormungandr, and Hel**
Loki's three monstrous children with the giantess Angrboda of the Iron Wood. Fenrir is the great wolf who kills Odin at Ragnarok, Jormungandr is the Midgard Serpent that Odin threw into the ocean surrounding the world, and Hel, who is half blue and half flesh-colored, rules the underworld of the dishonorable dead, to which Odin sent her.

**Lokasenna**
"Loki's Quarrel" or "Loki's Flyting," a poem in the Poetic Edda (Codex Regius) set at a feast held by the sea giant Aegir. Loki kills Aegir's servant Fimafeng for being praised, is driven out, then returns and trades insults with every god and goddess (including accusations of incest and of effeminate sorcery) until Thor threatens to smite him.

**Escaping as a salmon**
After the Lokasenna, Loki fled and hid in a house with four doors, often transforming into a salmon at Franang's Falls. He invented the fishing net, then burned it when the gods approached, but the gods used its ashes to make their own net and caught him in salmon form.

**The bet with Brokkr and Sindri**
After cutting off the golden hair of Thor's wife Sif, Loki had the Sons of Ivaldi make her new hair along with other treasures such as the folding ship Skidbladnir. He then bet his head that the dwarves Brokkr and Sindri (Eitri) could not make better gifts, and turned into a fly to sting Brokkr, which caused Mjolnir's handle to come out short. Loki lost the bet but avoided beheading by arguing he had never wagered his neck, so Brokkr sewed his lips shut instead.

**Idunn and Thiazi**
When the giant Thiazi, in eagle form, seized Loki (who had struck him with a pole), Loki agreed to lure the goddess Idunn and her apples of immortality out of Asgard. When the gods began to age, Loki rescued her by borrowing a falcon-feather cloak and turning her into a nut; Thiazi chased him in eagle form and was burned to death by a fire at Asgard's walls. To compensate Thiazi's daughter Skadi, Loki made her laugh by tying his testicles to the beard of a goat.

**Eating contest against Logi**
While traveling with Thor to the hall of the giant Utgard-Loki, Loki competed in an eating contest against Logi, who devoured not only the meat but the bones and the trough. Logi was later revealed to be fire itself in disguise.

**Killed by Heimdall at Ragnarok**
At the end of the world, Loki breaks free and leads the giants against the gods, and he and the watchman god Heimdall kill each other. Earlier, Loki and Heimdall fought in the form of seals over Freya's necklace Brisingamen, which Loki had stolen and Heimdall recovered.

**Thokk**
A giantess, presumed to be Loki in disguise, who was the only being that refused to weep for Baldr. Hel had agreed to release Baldr if everything in the world mourned him, so Thokk's refusal ("Let Hel hold what she has") kept Baldr in the underworld.

**Otr and Andvari's gold**
While traveling with Odin and Hoenir, Loki killed an otter with a stone; it was actually Otr, son of the sorcerer Hreidmar. To pay the wergild (blood money) of filling and covering the otter's skin with red gold, Loki borrowed a net from the sea goddess Ran, caught the dwarf Andvari, and extorted his treasure and cursed ring. This story opens the Volsunga saga.

**Thor's journey to Thrym**
When the giant Thrym stole Mjolnir and demanded Freya as a bride, Loki accompanied Thor to Jotunheim with Thor disguised as Freya and Loki as her maid. Loki explained away Thor's huge appetite and fiery eyes until Thor recovered his hammer.

**Naglfar**
The ship made from the fingernails and toenails of the dead, which sails against the gods at Ragnarok. Loki stands at its helm in some accounts.

**Farbauti and Laufey**
Loki's parents, the giant Farbauti and Laufey (also called Nal), which makes Loki part giant despite living among the Aesir. His brothers are Helblindi and Byleistr, and he is also called Lopt.
